title: Distilled equations predicted instability in simulated multi-planet systems
summary: Researchers distilled a neural network trained on three-planet simulations into compact equations for orbital instability time. Tested on previously simulated five-planet systems, the equations captured changes of orders of magnitude near strong orbital resonances. A systematic error remained for closely spaced planets.
ai_technology: Sparse neural feature learning; PySR symbolic regression
organization: Cornell University; MIT; Harvey Mudd College; University of Cambridge

source_review.scope: Model equations, Results, Figures 2–4, Appendices A–C and physical interpretation

evidence.tested: The equation used sparse statistics from short numerical integrations. It was tested on held-out three-planet simulations and on an existing five-planet grid under a neighboring-trio approximation.
evidence.unknown: The five-planet grid used equal masses and circular coplanar orbits. Results are approximate predictions of simulated dynamics, with compressed prediction ranges and no observational validation.
evidence.ai_role: The network learned sparse combinations of orbital elements. PySR converted its predicted instability times into closed-form expressions over those learned variables.
